plot: The morning after camping Grandma teaches Max to ride her old blue scooter in the park, but every ride turns left into the bush or the pond and Max blames the scooter; his aim-right plan ends in the muddy pond edge, until Bird watches from the tree and sees Max's head turns to the ducks he waves at, so Max learns the scooter goes where he looks, rides straight to Grandma's red ball, and finds her Halloween costume box with floppy dog ears.

script.title: Why Does Max's Scooter Only Go Left?

beats.say: Whoa! Whoa! Left again! Why does this scooter only go LEFT?
Max! Watch out for the bushes! Too late. Crunch!
Ten rides. Ten times into the same bush. Why?
This morning started so well. Grandma's old blue scooter came out.
I rode this scooter when I was little. Now it's your turn.
Easy! One paw on, one paw push. Zoom!
Max looks around the park. The ducks are by the pond.
Hello, ducks! Watch me! I'm going to be fast!
Max loves the ducks. He waves at them every single morning.
Grandma made a path with cones. Ride straight to the big tree.
Straight to the tree. No problem. Here I go!
Push. Push. The scooter rolls... and turns left.
Max is in the bush! Only his tail is sticking out!
I'm okay! The bush is soft. Pointy, but soft.
Wobbly at first is normal, dear. Try again.
Max tries again. And again. Left. Left. Always left.
This scooter is broken! It only knows one way!
Let me check the wheel. It spins fine. Look.
Then the scooter just doesn't like me. Not one bit.
If it ends in the pond, it goes back to the shed.
Back to the shed? No! I have to ride it straight!
I have a plan. If it goes left, I aim right!
Aim right to go straight? That's so silly it might work!
Max points the scooter far to the right. Push. Push.
It's working! It's going right! Look, ducks! Look at me!
Max waves at the ducks. And the scooter turns. Left.
Right into the muddy edge of the pond. Wet paws!
The ducks are laughing! Quack, quack, quack!
Even my plan goes left! This scooter is a duck scooter!
Oh dear. Wet paws. Maybe that's enough for today.
No, please! One more ride! I almost had it!
Wait. Before we give up, let's test the scooter alone.
Alone? A scooter can't ride by itself, Mouse.
One big push. Nobody on it. Let's see where it goes.
Max gives the empty scooter one big push. Off it rolls.
It rolls straight past the cones. All the way to Grandma's feet.
It goes straight without me? Then... it's not broken?
So the scooter is fine. Something about YOU makes it turn!
Me? But I'm doing everything right! Paw on, paw push!
One last ride, dear. Then the scooter goes home to the shed.
Bird flies up into the big tree to think.
From up here, I can see the whole park. Ride once more!
Max pushes off one more time. Bird watches from above.
Max's head turns to the ducks. Then his paws turn too.
Stop! I saw it! I saw what makes you go left!
What? A rock? A bad wheel? A sneaky duck?
It's your eyes, Max! You always look at the ducks!
Your head turns to them. Then your body follows. Whoosh, left!
My eyes? The scooter goes where I look?
Bird is right. A scooter follows your eyes, dear.
So the scooter was never broken. I was just saying hello!
Then look at something that isn't a duck.
Okay. Grandma, stand by the big tree. I'll look only at you.
Grandma stands by the tree and holds up a red ball.
Eyes on the ball. Eyes on Grandma. Not on the ducks.
Push. Push. The scooter wobbles. Then it rolls straight.
Past the first cone. Past the second cone. Straight, straight!
I did it! I rode all the way to the big tree!
Beautiful! You ride better than I did at your age.
Okay, now you can say hello to the ducks. Slowly!
Hello, ducks! I'm riding to you on purpose this time!
Max stops right by the pond. Not one paw gets wet.
Look where you want to go. Then you get there.
That works for scooters. And for lots of other things too.
On the way home, Max rides the scooter in front of everyone.
Grandma, what is in that big box by your door?
My old costume box. Tomorrow is Halloween, you know!
Max peeks inside the box. He sees floppy brown dog ears.
Dog ears? Grandma... I have the silliest idea ever.
